source_title: Commercial LPG Cylinder Prices Hiked By Rs 10 Ahead Of Diwali; Check City-Wise Rates
source_excerpt:
Commercial LPG cylinder prices have been increased by Rs 10-11.50 across major cities from November 1, giving hotels, restaurants, dhabas and catering businesses a slight cost shock just ahead of Diwali.
The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder in Delhi has gone up by Rs 10 to Rs 2,820. In Mumbai, the cylinder is now priced at Rs 2,774.50 after a similar increase.
Kolkata has also witnessed a Rs 10 hike, taking the price of a commercial cylinder to Rs 2,964. In Chennai, the increase is Rs 11.50, with the new price standing at Rs 2,994.50.
In Bengaluru, commercial LPG cylinder prices have risen by Rs 10 to Rs 2,908.

The increase is expected to add to operating costs for businesses that depend on commercial LPG cylinders, particularly hotels, restaurants, roadside eateries and catering services.

While commercial LPG consumers will have to pay more, domestic consumers have received relief, with no change in the price of the 14.2-kg household LPG cylinder from November 1.
Meanwhile, a new connection for a 5-kg Free Trade LPG (FTL) cylinder now costs Rs 1,903, while a refill is priced at Rs 782, according to the revised rate list.
The latest increase follows successive upward revisions during the festive season. Commercial LPG prices were raised marginally on September 1, followed by a Rs 65 per cylinder hike on October 1.
The November 1 revision has increased rates by another Rs 10 to Rs 17 across metropolitan cities, with the Delhi price reaching Rs 2,820.
Earlier in the year, commercial LPG prices had witnessed sharp fluctuations. A steep increase of nearly Rs 1,000 per cylinder on May 1 pushed the Delhi rate above Rs 3,000 to around Rs 3,071.50.
Oil marketing companies subsequently announced cumulative price cuts of Rs 380 per cylinder in July and August, offering relief to commercial consumers during the summer months.

The volatility in LPG prices during 2026 has been linked in the report to geopolitical tensions and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, a key maritime route for crude oil and LPG shipments from the Middle East.
India imports roughly half of its natural gas and LPG consumption, with a significant share of its LPG supplies originating from Gulf producers and passing through the Strait.
Operational bottlenecks and heightened security risks in the waterway earlier this year reportedly reduced global LPG supply and pushed up freight costs.
Higher shipping risk premiums, fluctuations in global crude prices and elevated international Saudi Aramco contract prices have also contributed to domestic commercial fuel costs.
The report noted that Brent crude was hovering above $110 per barrel, adding to the pressure on fuel prices.
